title: Traffic telemetry decision log for credential exfiltration and staged containment
content:
Context and purpose:
This note captures our working decisions and detection heuristics after the October–November low-and-slow credential harvesting run that gradually consumed per-tenant quotas across multiple regions. It's intentionally informal — a field log to: record queries we used to spot the pattern, the staggered mitigation steps we exercised, and remaining follow-ups before we turn this into a formal runbook.

Summary of the incident (short):
- Attack pattern: attacker obtained a small set of API keys (likely from a public repo or leaked integration) and performed long-tail requests that mimicked legitimate traffic but at elevated per-key rate for a subset of endpoints (embeddings + rerank).
- Effect: slow quota depletion per-customer, spiky errors as tenants hit soft and hard caps at different times, downstream retries amplified traffic.
- Timeframe: 2025-10-15 to 2025-11-03 detection window; active mitigation phase 2025-10-22 to 2025-11-07.
- Impact: transient latency increases for affected tenants, elevated error rates (429/503) for a handful of high-value customers, increased cost due to retries. No data exfiltration confirmed from audit logs, but we treated credential compromise as probable.

What made detection hard (lessons):
- Low-and-slow pattern blended into normal traffic, per-key metrics didn't exceed absolute thresholds early on.
- Backoff and retry clients from customers reintroduced bursts that looked like legitimate spikes.
- Some customers had multiple keys and cross-key smoothing masked per-key anomalies in aggregated views.
- WAF rules were tuned for volumetric DDoS and didn't flag the request shapes used (many small post bodies, valid model inputs).

Telemetry queries that found it (examples, adapt for current metrics pipeline):
- Per-api-key rolling 1h qps: SELECT api_key, rate( count() ) FROM requests WHERE timestamp > now()-1h GROUP BY api_key HAVING rate > (customer_baseline*3)
- Ratio of endpoint mix per key: count_by_endpoint(api_key, last_24h) — look for skew to embeddings/rerank > 70%
- KV-cache miss rate by key (proxy for repeated cold prompts): compute middleware.cache_miss_rate(api_key, 24h) > 0.6
- Unusual geographic dispersion: distinct_regions(api_key, 24h) > expected for that customer
- Error amplification signal: watch for increasing retry rate per user-agent between 5–60s intervals

Quick detection dashboard widgets we added (ad-hoc):
- Top 25 keys by 24h token spend with axis for soft-cap age
- Heatmap: per-key endpoint ratio (embedding vs chat vs generation)
- Replayable sample requests: store a sanitized sample per key for signature analysis

Immediate mitigations exercised (ordered and why):
1) Soft-step throttles: initially increased open telemetry alerting and applied a 40% down-sampling for suspected keys to reduce cost and observe behavior. Rationale: reduce noise and gather clearer signal without breaking customers.
2) Apply per-key incremental hard caps (temporary): set hard cap of 2x baseline for keys that trip endpoint-skew and miss-rate heuristics. Rationale: limit damage while preserving most legitimate traffic.
3) Evaluate token rotation: for keys with clear evidence of compromise (confirmation via customer or repeated anomalous IPs), recommend rotation and suspend old key after handshake.
4) WAF quick signatures: introduce request-shape rules (small text submission rate over window) — set to log-only for 48h then move to block for confirmed patterns.
5) Global retry-suppression: introduce short-lived global backoff for clients causing retry storms (early experiments: add jitter to 503s at edge).

Commands and ops snippets used during triage (examples):
- List top keys by tokens last 24h (CLI): rwi metrics query "top api_key by sum(tokens) where timestamp>now()-24h" --limit=50
- Block IP in perimeter: rwi waf block add --ip 18.23.45.67 --reason "credential-harvest-pattern" --ttl 24h
- Apply per-key hard cap: rwi keys update --key abcd-1234 --hard-cap-tokens 500000 --note "temp cap for suspected compromise"

Role handoffs and communications:
- SRE lead (oncall) — triage and apply per-key caps, coordinate customer comms
- Account security — contact tenants with suspected compromised keys, request rotation
- DevRel/SE — prepare key rotation quickstart for customers
- Product/Policy — review thresholds to ensure we don't deny service inadvertently

False positive concerns and mitigations:
- Busy-machine-learning customers legitimately have skewed endpoint usage. Mitigate by cross-checking billing spike alerts and contacting customer before aggressive block.
- Cross-key smoothing: require signal from at least two orthogonal heuristics (endpoint skew + cache miss + geography) before automated hard cap.

Proposed detection heuristic (short):
- Trigger if: (A) endpoint-skew >= 70% embeddings or rerank over 24h AND (B) cache_miss_rate >= 0.5 AND (C) qps increased > 2x baseline for 1h AND (D) new remote ASN or distinct IP cohort not previously seen for this tenant.
- Action: create auto-ticket, notify oncall, set soft cap at 1.5x baseline; if behavior persists for 3h escalate to manual hard cap + customer contact.

Staged key rotation playbook (for SRE + CS):
1) Confirm: check audit log for put-key/create-key events, look for suspicious git references, and confirm with customer if possible.
2) Provision new key in staging and ask customer to switch in low-traffic window. Provide quick commands and SDK snippet.
3) Monitor new-key vs old-key metrics for 2h; if new-key matches old behavior, escalate (likely attacker has access to code repo or CI).
4) Revoke old key after successful cutover, collect for forensics.

WAF signature notes (working):
- Signature 1: repeated small POSTs (<400 bytes) to /v1/embedding with consistent header fingerprints but varying bodies — log-only initially.
- Signature 2: high entropy in Authorization header usage patterns across many IPs — correlate with stolen-token list.
- Danger: blocking too early will affect SDK customers using small batched inputs; prefer graduated enforcement.

Post-incident action items (backlog):
- Turn the above heuristics into a formal runbook with playbook steps and clickable console actions (owner: Liam).
- Implement automated two-signal gating before auto-hard-cap (owner: Deepak, due 2026-03-01).
- Create an SDK best-practice doc for customers about securing keys and rotating automatically (owner: Marina).
- Add a telemetry daily job to recalc per-tenant baseline every 24h to adapt to growth (owner: observability infra).

Open questions / unresolved:
- How do we balance tenant experience with automatic rotation enforcement when we have high confidence but no customer confirmation? (policy)
- Is 3 hours the right escalation window or should it be shorter for high-cost endpoints? Need cost model analysis.
- Should we expand the WAF rule set to include small-body rate heuristics in block mode for new customers only? (risk of false positive)

Notes-to-self / quick timeline log (raw):
- 2025-10-22 09:14 — first anomalous qps observed on key abcd-1234; escalation created SRE-4219
- 2025-10-22 12:03 — applied temp soft-sampling 40% on abcd-1234; observed reduced downstream retries
- 2025-10-25 18:44 — contacted tenant, tenant rotated one key (partial remediation)
- 2025-10-28 03:20 — new keys from same tenant showed similar behavior -> likely CI integration compromised
- 2025-11-03 07:50 — deployed log-only WAF shape signature; captured samples for forensics

Appendix: quick checklist for oncall when a low-and-slow harvest is suspected:
- [ ] Pull per-key 24h endpoint mix and token spend
- [ ] Compute cache miss rates per-key
- [ ] Check distinct ASN/IP cohorts for sudden expansion
- [ ] Apply soft-sample throttle (20–50%) while investigating
- [ ] Open support ticket and contact customer security if tenant identifiable
- [ ] If confirmed compromise: provision new key, and schedule revocation of old key after verification

If this looks reasonable we should convert to a formal runbook and post to Confluence. For now keep iterations here and I'll update with new query snippets and rule text once we test more variants.

-- Aisha
